title: Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valas
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: A great man in Rabbi’s time, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:1: he had a garment worth three hundred thousand dinars and gave it to Rabbi, who found kilayim in it and burned it. In Gittin 6:7: “Rabbi Hillel bar Valas asked before Rabbi” (and there it is explicit that the reference is to our holy Rabbi). Likewise in Gittin 59a he said: “From the days of Moses until Rabbi we have not found Torah and greatness in one place.” In Avodah Zarah 52b he resolves the words of Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi, which he had raised as a difficulty to Rabbi; and there, 53a, he explains the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya.

He likewise received from his father Rabbi Valas, as in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, end of chapter 2: “Rabbi Yonah said: Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valas went out to the market; they asked him … he came and asked his father,” etc. In Kilayim, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1: “Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Chiyya bar Va: They found written in the notebook of Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Alas” (Hyman identifies Alas with the Babylonian Talmud’s Valas). In Challah 1:3: “Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Chama bar Ukva: Rabbi Hillel ben Hali (Hyman proposes Valas) attributed it to Rabbi Yehudah.” From this, the Raza”f (Zecharias Frankel) concluded in his precious book Mavo HaYerushalmi [1] that Hillel belonged to the third generation. Hyman rejects this, arguing, as above, that Hillel was among Rabbi’s students. What Rav Chama bar Ukva said in his name is no proof, for Rabbi Chama bar Ukva said only that Rabbi Hillel attributed it to Rabbi Yehudah. Hyman suggests that possibly what we find in Beitzah 5:2, “Rabbi Lil son of Rabbi Alas,” is Rabbi Hillel son of Rabbi Valas.

notes.text: Missing footnote[1] after MavoHaYerushalmi is a genuine source hold on p002; do not invent it from the Gemara. רז״פ designates the cited work’s author, ZechariasFrankel, as disclosed in the original note. Hyman’s chronological objection, Alas/Valas/Hali/Lil variants and possible identity remain attributed.

The supplied [1] after Mavo HaYerushalmi has no supplied footnote; its contents are not recovered here. רז״פ is rendered as the cited work’s author, Zecharias Frankel, as disclosed in the original draft note. Hyman rejects the proposed third-generation placement and offers the Alas/Valas, Hali/Valas and possible Lil identifications; these remain his arguments rather than a merged identity or newly verified chronology. The full 300,000-dinar figure and the father/son directions are preserved.

[1] The Wikisource transcription’s note points to Frankel’s Mavo HaYerushalmi, p. 76b (עו:). The note marker is absent from Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 375). In the consulted digital transcription of Frankel, he suggests a third-generation date because of Rabbi Chama bar Ukva and also proposes reading Hillel for Lil. Hyman expressly disputes the dating. The earlier notes record the state of the citation before this review.

The consulted Gittin 59a gives Hillel as an alternative to Rabbah son of Rava for the saying about Torah and greatness. In Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:1, Rabbi Yose reports the notebook wording in the name of Rabbi Chiyya bar Va. Rabbi Yonah reports a version about the wall in the same teacher’s name. Hyman’s printed entry includes the wall report. The supplied text includes the notebook alone. Challah 1:3 reads Halis, whereas the supplied Hyman text has Hali and proposes Valas. Beitzah 5:2 has Lil son of Alles. The name identifications remain conjectures.
